newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX ACCESS energy futures up amid revised APIs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX ACCESS energy futures up amid revised APIs.

text.p: Prices for U.S. energy futures edged up during ACCESS trade Tuesday, with light trade allowing locals to push up products and a revised crude oil draw putting a bullish edge on the contract, traders said.
"Last week, we showed a 11 million (barrrel) draw," a trader said, noting the draw was first reported as nine million barrels.
"So (this week) it's not as big a build as it looks," he added.

U.S. crude oil stocks held in primary storage rose 4.65 million barrels last week to 289.46 million. But that build is added to a revised 284.82 million barrels, a smaller amount of supply than initially reported.
After falling eight cents in daytime trade, February NYMEX crude firmed 17 cents to $25.28 a barrel after-hours. About 653 lots traded in the front month and 1,507 overall.
NYMEX February heating oil firmed slightly to 70.10 cents a barrel, up 0.68 cents a gallon from the settle as a light 209 lots traded in February and 287 changed hands for all months.
Gasoline futures edged up 0.46 cents a gallon to 67.50 cents a gallon, with activity gauged at 40 lots traded in February and a weak 87 traded in total.
